cards.text: Breaking it Down: The Five Stages of Business The "five stages of business" theory is a popular one because it's accurate at predicting the trajectory of a healthy and sustainable business. Of course, these stages refer to that company's growth with "growth" defined as an increase in both size and complexity. Why Your Company Needs to Grow There's a popular saying I often refer to when describing growth, "businesses grow to their own level of incompetence." Putting that simply, you grow to the level you aim for; it doesn't happen on accident. What is growth? It might not be what you think.
cards.title: Five Stages of Business reference 1

cards.text: To many owners, growth can be a daunting prospect. To them, it means more work, more stress, and being spread too thin. However, positive growth is shared among your workforce where key people are identified, coached to take leadership roles, and ultimately means less work for you as the owner. Stage One: The Owner Does It All Maybe you're at this stage currently. Or maybe you think back to a "simpler time" when you were the star employee of your business and, for the most part, did all of the work yourself.
cards.title: Five Stages of Business reference 2

cards.text: While this may be an exciting start to a venture, it's not a sustainable one for these reasons: • You can't compete on price against similar businesses with more resources • The constant ebb and flow of your cash flow creates added stress • Peripheral jobs like marketing aren't given the attention they need • As the owner, you're working well over 40 hours a week At this stage, your success is contingent upon how hard you're willing to work. You must rely on a GP margin to protect profitability, developing systematic habits, and good time management to turn a consistent profit.
cards.title: Five Stages of Business reference 3

cards.text: Most businesses will stall here; only the great ones continue on. Stage Two: The Business Begins to Outgrow the Owner This stage is perhaps the scariest of them all. Suddenly, a business owner who is a skilled tradesperson is finding that their workload is exceeding what they can reasonably and accurately achieve. How do you go from a person good at a trade to a manager of people? The two ideas do not easily overlap.
cards.title: Five Stages of Business reference 4

cards.text: Yet, you need to begin to step back from the day-to-day production and service duties and begin to coach people to embody your spirit; the very same spirit that made you a success in the first place. Stage two is all about building a structure that is both systematic and scalable. You need to put in place systems and practices that place employees in the driver's seat. Hiring more employees should not dilute your quality; it should extrapolate it.
cards.title: Five Stages of Business reference 5

cards.text: These are the common pitfalls I see at this stage: • The owner feels a loss of control as their need to delegate increases • Anxiety over control forces the owner to come back into the fray and begin micromanaging • Overhead creeps up as profits decrease while training occurs On the other hand, a successful stage two is one where employees completely and enthusiastically understand their responsibilities and goals. Furthermore, the production crew is as reliable, accurate, and detail-oriented as you were and the sales team demonstrates an ability to close new business.
cards.title: Five Stages of Business reference 6

cards.text: At this stage, you should finally be able to start looking 1-2 years out instead of day-by-day or month-to-month. Stage Three: Employees Become Self-Managed, Complexity Increases At stage three, the look and feel of how a business operates should be profoundly different than in stage one but with a similar company culture that made it initially successful. As the workforce increases and becomes skilled at their jobs so too does the complexity of the service. As the owner, you've found that you're most needed as a leader and mentor. You captain the ship without really going below deck.
cards.title: Five Stages of Business reference 7

cards.text: Meetings become streamlined, task-driven, and extremely productive with a key employee from each team managing their individual department. The most common dangers at this stage: • Continued micromanagement creates a fearful culture; employees are afraid to think creatively or to even speak up • Benchmarks are not established that have clear, measurable metrics; meeting quality suffers since no one can easily explain their successes or challenges • Lack of inspiration creates a spiral effect often forcing the company to regress into stage two Trust is through the roof; the owner knows that key people are in place at every functional level. High-level debriefing is all that's needed.
cards.title: Five Stages of Business reference 8

cards.text: Mutual accountability and even cross-training occur naturally. Most of all, the owner is seen as a coach and a mentor. Stage Four: Business is Completely Independent of the Owner The time has finally come; if you see your business as your child, then this is perhaps the time that they go off to college. Things just work even when you're not actively engaged. The sales team is successful and completely independent, key managers are acting just as you were when the company was young; they're managing enthusiastically and effectively and completely understand the ebb and flow of the business. At this point, marketing should increase in its complexity.
cards.title: Five Stages of Business reference 9

cards.text: Your departments are now so distinct that they necessitate their own channels of outreach. As the owner, you're completely settled into the role of mentor and leader without any engagement with the daily operations of the company. Furthermore, the business is so fine-tuned that your annual review of company performance can be deeply researched, understood, and improved for next year. At stage four, nothing about your revenue stream is random.
cards.title: Five Stages of Business reference 10

cards.text: Here are the dangers at this stage: • If trust isn't sufficiently built, then the owner will have trouble "letting go" in response to the new management team • Sales are not predictable enough to forecast growth; the next year is always unclear • The business suffers an identity crisis because it fails to fill the void as the owner steps back Success in this space happens when middle management is inspired by the owner and, ultimately, transcends the original vision. Sales are so predictable that forecasts can be made 1-2 years out, which builds peace-of-mind and cultivates a culture of boundary-pushing.
cards.title: Five Stages of Business reference 11

cards.text: Most of all, as the owner you can take 1-2 weeks off and feel like the company is running just fine without you. Stage Five: The Owner Doesn't Have to Know Everything Stage five is truly the end game. As the original owner, you're more-or-less functioning at an advisory capacity. You may still be the face of the company and you may even schmooze with certain clients but there is much about the operation of the business that you're no longer aware of because you trust your departments. By now, you're not just a leader; you're a skilled mentor and coach that people look up to.
cards.title: Five Stages of Business reference 12

cards.text: Your high-level vision drives the company. You inspire people directly, either through the way you lead the company or through business retreats and training. As with all stages, stage 5 has its own list of dangers to look out for: • You disengage from the company too early, leaving a rift that hasn't been mended by cultivating a strong team of middle managers • The message, culture, and mission of the company are too muddled.
cards.title: Five Stages of Business reference 13

cards.text: Like a game of telephone, it only gets worse as time goes on • Meetings are not streamlined due to poorly framed metrics, wasting time and making productivity suffer A Great Business Stands on its Own Two Feet From day one, your goal as a business owner should be to get your company situated so it can stand on its own two feet. If you want your company to outlast you or, even better, be your legacy, then you need to structure it in a way that it remains successful even when you're gone.
cards.title: Five Stages of Business reference 14

cards.text: Each of the five stages is contingent upon one thing; steering the ship but giving your team the time, space, and trust that they need to do their part. As they grow your responsibilities should shrink. Soon enough, you should find that it functions without you! At GNA Inc., this is what we're always trying to achieve for our clients. We want to give you autonomy, peace of mind, and pride in what you've created.

cards.text: It's one thing to drive your business to profitable levels of success. It's quite another thing to keep it going year after year. After working with Contractors for over 20 years, I've learned there are three challenges that cause most business owners to lose power in their day-to-day operations. When you lose power in your operations, it costs you money. The fact of the matter is every business is operated by people and these people have attitudes, emotions and sometimes conflicting points of view. Often times, this can seriously get in the way of your employee's productivity. So, here are the three challenges to overcome so you can sustain your profits for years to come.
cards.title: Three Challenges That Kill Productivity reference 1

cards.text: Gossip is the number one killer of productivity in your workplace. People waste more time and energy on who said what to who or who did or didn't do the right thing at the right time. This kind of gossip kills your employees' productivity and your business's ability to make money. Unneeded, unnecessary drama is an enormous waste of time and money! I really don't want your company to experience this so here's how to eliminate gossip. Straight talk means to take whatever issue someone is experiencing to the person they have an issue with. It is a commitment to no drama and instead a focus on pure productivity. This requires professionals to act like the adult professionals they are.
cards.title: Three Challenges That Kill Productivity reference 2

cards.text: It's about being honest, and nothing gets people back to work faster than saying the truth. Chances are whatever was a "problem" was all just a misunderstanding and a breakdown in communication somewhere along the line. Or you may find out one person appreciates the honest feedback because they had no idea or any intention towards hurting another person or you may uncover an undisclosed problem that can now be addressed directly. When one of your employees has a problem with someone make sure they take it right to the person they have an issue with. They do not need to get other parties involved because this usually creates gossip and wastes a lot of time and mental bandwidth.
cards.title: Three Challenges That Kill Productivity reference 3

cards.text: Expedites communication Save enormous amounts of time Increases productivity Teaches people who may be afraid of being confrontational how to resolve problems without your help Gives the listener valuable feedback Help your employees to maintain successful working partnerships One of the significant indicators of health I see in successful companies is people being at work, focused, on task. Another challenge that is critically important to your business's profits is sales. A problem I see many businesses make is not having all employees take ownership for the sales process. This may look like your team waiting around for the phone to ring or depending on Third Party Programs to generate more sales opportunities, or the weather.
cards.title: Three Challenges That Kill Productivity reference 4

cards.text: The real problem here starts by allowing your employees to believe selling belongs to someone else. When you hear your employees say any version of something like, "You're responsible for selling and I'm not," this is a really big problem because it's indicative of a laziness and lack of accountability in your business's culture. You need to help your employees understand everyone sells. Every employee should take on the attitude and practice of selling. When this happens the financial health of your company increases significantly. Here's how to shift your employees to understand everyone sells: Help them understand how they can exceed expectations of your customers with exceptional service.
cards.title: Three Challenges That Kill Productivity reference 5

cards.text: Help them understand the importance of returning phone calls as fast as possible. Put procedures in place so you can push work through your production pipelines as fast as possible and of course, do a great job in selling. The bottom line of this shift is getting all your employees on board to do whatever they can each day to reach out and invite new customers into a working relationship with you and take care of existing customers by working hard to exceed their expectations. If you don't have a sales process in place, I highly recommend Sandler.
cards.title: Three Challenges That Kill Productivity reference 6

cards.text: Have all your staff fully trained on it so they can demonstrate each step of the sales process anywhere, anytime and to anyone. This one practice alone can be enough to enormously impact the success and profits of your business. The last place where you may be losing power in your day-to-day operations is your employees lacking personal ownership. If your staff is just showing up to do their part, do what they are told, or just want to put in their time and have an attitude and unwillingness to look at anything outside of their job description, your likely experiencing a drag and loss in productivity. This type of culture will cost you lots of money over the years.
cards.title: Three Challenges That Kill Productivity reference 7

cards.text: If you're the type of business owner who feels this type of business culture isn't that big of a deal and thinks this is how all employees think, I'm willing to bet you don't realize how good you can actually have it. I want you to have the best. You deserve it, so let's go to work on this… The reality of business today is you not only need people who are highly productive, who think on their feet, but you need leaders. You need leaders who inspire others to lead, and you need these type of leaders at all levels in your business.
cards.title: Three Challenges That Kill Productivity reference 8

cards.text: I have seen Mitigation service technicians making marketing calls to insurance agents or out selling fire jobs and board ups. I have seen customer service coordinators driving sales and closing work for the whole production team through their efforts of tracking and cheering the team! I have even seen Estimators and Project Managers drive educational and cross training efforts with all their sub-contractors and for the whole team. cards.text: Mastermind Groups are tailored to your industry, challenges and goals. For Business Owners who want to go to the next level. People who come together on a regular basis to share their goals, workshop new ideas, get perspective and feedback from other smart, equally ambitious peers, and discover new resources they would not have found on their own. By getting the perspective and wisdom of the others in a peer-to-peer setting, a mastermind group helps each member to expand their thinking, move beyond their own personal world experience, and move towards achieving their own ambitions more quickly and easily than any of us can on our own.
cards.title: Mastermind Groups reference 1

cards.text: A commitment to confidentiality The first benefit of a mastermind group is a commitment to confidentiality. For any mastermind group to be successful, people need to trust that what they are sharing stays in the group. This simple (but not always easy) agreement means people can get to the heart of real issues quickly and find solutions faster. A commitment to good communication Good communication means members share their stories, experiences, and ideas-but they don't share advice. This may sound counterintuitive to some: Isn't advice what lets people make better decisions?
cards.title: Mastermind Groups reference 2

cards.text: As it turns out, people learn best when we share stories and experiences we've had with similar situations and challenges. Advice doesn't make that same connection or help people find solutions for themselves as easily as hearing the story of another member. A commitment to active participation This is a big one. The last benefit of a mastermind group is that it acts as an accountability group, where each member is committed to active participation. Your group will only work if each member is willing to regularly be involved.
cards.title: Mastermind Groups reference 3

cards.text: These foundational agreements are essential to creating the phenomenal results so many of us get from being a part of a mastermind group. Groups are designed to provide a continuous learning environment with discussions led by industry experts, Greg Neil, President of GNA, Inc. and Senior Associate John McPhillips Connect Monthly confidential meetings with business owners and general managers who will challenge assumptions and find out what is limiting your success. This means both sharing their opportunities and challenges openly, but also collaborating closely with other members as they navigate their own situations, situations where hearing the stories and experiences of others leads to breakthroughs.
cards.title: Mastermind Groups reference 4

cards.text: Network You get as much unbiased feedback as possible on your business challenges. Optimize We will work together towards one common goal - to make better decisions to benefit your company and employees, yourself, your family and your community. Accelerate Your Chair, who facilitates your group meetings, will also meet with you one-on-one to hold you accountable for meeting your goals. Events and calendar integration Mastermind groups only work with regularly scheduled in-person or live video virtual meetings. These meetings typically last 60-90 minutes and enable a member to discuss their current challenges and/or opportunities with other members offering their own related stories and experiences that may be helpful.
cards.title: Mastermind Groups reference 5

cards.text: Live video meetings on ZOOM Offering your mastermind group virtually means that you can pull together a much more diverse and interesting set of members. Group chat has a wide array of functionality, but most importantly its another tool in your toolbox for creating deep connections between your members. cards.text: Are you ready to discover the 2 challenges to seriously great employee performance? I'm going to give you two tips to make the day-to-day operations of your business a ton easier and more productive. Once you have these two things working for you in your business you'll have a business culture that drive continuous growth and success. It will also give you the kind of freedom you really deserve to have as a business owner. Over the years, I have seen many business owners struggling with employees who have un-coachable behaviors and they do not realize they are dealing with a level of dysfunction that is unfixable.
cards.title: Two Challenges to Great Employee Performance reference 1

cards.text: Maybe you get sucked into trying to keep the employee around because it seems like it's the right thing to do, yet the longer you hold off on firing the employee, the worse their productivity is and the more you seem to just tolerate it. Not only is this really frustrating, it's also damaging and expensive to your business. The best example I can think of for this is Steven Curry, one of the hottest basketball stars in the NBA and a player for the Golden State Warriors. Maybe you're wondering and asking yourself, what does being coachable actually look like? When someone is coachable, the coach says do this and they do it. No argument.
cards.title: Two Challenges to Great Employee Performance reference 2

cards.text: A coachable person is also committed to making the coach right. A coachable person is also responsible for making sure their own execution is accurate. In the case of Steven Curry, he practices what the coach says to do over and over again until he got his skill sets down perfectly. So how does this look in your business and with your employees? Coachable behavior in your business can look like you employees asking you for help on a particular specific situation. They take responsibility for their own education and come to you asking for coaching on something. Then your employee's practice what you offer with a commitment to having it work.
cards.title: Two Challenges to Great Employee Performance reference 3

cards.text: Isn't this the kind of behavior you really want from your employees? You deserve it and it is key to you having a highly successful and profitable business. Have you ever had a situation where you had a loyal employee who has been with you for years, they were trained and knew how to do their job yet, their productivity was really low? How can you get this person to increase their productivity? Real accountability is another way of saying, get their buy in. Let me make this plain and simple because this is a powerful tool to help your employees get focused.
cards.title: Two Challenges to Great Employee Performance reference 4

cards.text: This is critically important because real accountability is a personal choice. It's not you forcing them to complete a task. If you are forcing people to do things, your productivity will always be low over the long-term. But when you give your employees a choice and get their buy in, they will jump through hoops to hit the goals because they feel that were part of the decision making process. When you can get their buy in, they will have more trust and respect for you because you have trust and respect for them by asking for their buy in. This is the difference between being a boss and a leader. That's a whole topic in and of itself.
cards.title: Two Challenges to Great Employee Performance reference 5

cards.text: The problem is too many business owners don't get their employees buy in and/or they assume the employee has already made a choice. When this happens your employees feel burdened with choice they didn't make and they start to resent and resist you. This then leads to a situation where you feel like you have to push them harder to get anything done. This is why I want you to get your employees to buy in to what needs to happen in your business. I have never encountered an employee who when given a choice didn't choose their own accountabilities. Give people a choice to choose their own accountabilities and they will step up to meet their expectations every time.
cards.title: Two Challenges to Great Employee Performance reference 6

cards.text: In fact, when given the choice, you will be surprised at how willing your employees are to take on whatever accountabilities they need to make things work for everyone. Now that you understand a bit on these two barriers that are stopping you from greater productivity and profitability, let me offer you something that I promise will take your business to the next level. cards.text: How To Push Past the 3 Barriers That Stop Most Contractors From Increasing Their Profits Do you know the 3 biggest barriers that block you from increasing your net profits, productivity and employee morale? If not, then read this immediately. Barrier #1: Finding and Keeping Good Help Finding and keeping good help these days can block you from growing your company and increasing your profits. If you don't get this handled, you will be staffing up with employees you don't really want, put up with less than desirable performance and suffer the financial consequences of doing so. I don't want this for you.
cards.title: Three Barriers That Stop Contractors from Profits reference 1

cards.text: A Personal Story: One time I was working in a company and we desperately needed a marketing person. We ran ads, collected resumes and no one was hired. When I asked what was going on, I was told no one good was applying. So, we waited and waited. Two weeks went by and still it seemed no good candidates. So, I asked for the stack of resumes and called every single one. The result was, we found an excellent person who was able to hit the ground running.
cards.title: Three Barriers That Stop Contractors from Profits reference 2

cards.text: What I learned was sometimes, there are really good people hiding behind an okay looking resume and you would never know that until you get them on the phone and meet them. If you're willing to do a little extra work, you can find and hire great people who will help explode the growth of your company. Here's the Real Problem: Many business owners believe you cannot find the right people because of their area, geography or economics and as a result, they don't even look, or they look, but, they already know how its going to turn out…..sure enough, they're right every time. Maybe you can relate to this?
cards.title: Three Barriers That Stop Contractors from Profits reference 3

cards.text: By buying into this type of thinking, you're defeated before even starting. I hear owners and managers all over the U.S. complaining about how they can't find good help these days. What I've learned is there isn't any more area more difficult than any other part of the U.S. The truth is finding good help can be challenging but it's not impossible. Here's How You Get Around This: The key to is having an effective hiring process.
cards.title: Three Barriers That Stop Contractors from Profits reference 4

cards.text: An effective hiring process starts with really good ad copy, follows with solid screening and interviewing practices and ends with hiring procedures that will simultaneously begin to build your management culture of highly accountable people. This way you have a team of people who will do the job and care about the project and your customers as much as you do Barrier #2: Not Keeping a Steady Flow of Work Coming In Sales is the life blood of your business. It's extremely important for your business to have marketing outreach practices to consistently provide a steady flow of leads for sales.
cards.title: Three Barriers That Stop Contractors from Profits reference 5

cards.text: What typically happens for most businesses, is they become dependent on the weather or TPA's and they wait for the phone to ring. They don't have an effective outreach program in place or if they do, it's not managed very well. Maybe you've made this mistake before? Maybe you don't understand how to set up an effective outreach program and/or you don't know what to expect from your marketing efforts? A Personal Story: One time I was asking a group of estimators to start marketing in a very successful business that historically had never done any marketing, at least not in their ten years of operations anyway.
cards.title: Three Barriers That Stop Contractors from Profits reference 6

cards.text: At first, they were good with this, then came the day they went 180 degrees the other way. All of a sudden, they experienced tons of resistance from their team and reality started to sink in. Two hours later, we discovered what we intended for marketing and what the employees thought marketing meant were two completely different things. Once I helped the business owner and their employees get on the same page, not only was everyone happy, but the discussion solidified the team around marketing practices and initiatives that no one had ever thought of before. As a result, their productivity and sales went up dramatically.
cards.title: Three Barriers That Stop Contractors from Profits reference 7

cards.text: Here's the Real Problem: One of the biggest problems I see contractors make is having too many employees thinking its someone else's job to go find work. This misunderstanding occurs because when you first hire someone, it was not made clear that they would be accountable for marketing and sales. It probably wasn't even mentioned at all from the beginning. So now this leaves you asking for them to market for you and you may be experiencing lots of resistance to this.
cards.title: Three Barriers That Stop Contractors from Profits reference 8

cards.text: Maybe your employee is saying, "You didn't hire me for that!" Here's How to Get Around This: You must learn to inspire an attitude in your company of "Everyone Sells, and everyone Markets Here, Everyone." The truth is your customers just want to speak with someone who has expertise on getting the jobs done. Once you learn to find and keep good help, you'll have the kind of expertise your customers really want. So then, all your employees need to do to effectively market is to be their shinning self and ask your customer or prospect if there is anything they need help with.
cards.title: Three Barriers That Stop Contractors from Profits reference 9

cards.text: Your employees need to be positive and mentally expect the prospect or customer to give you work immediately. It also helps if all your employees have some training in a sales process, but it's not completely necessary. Barrier #3: Maintaining a High Profit Margin on Each Job There can be so many variables going into the making of your gross profit performance when it comes to managing all of them. The reality is you have some estimators who write and sell, others who only produce, and then some who write and run. Without getting into a big argument here about which is the best of these, let's ask this question...
cards.title: Three Barriers That Stop Contractors from Profits reference 10

cards.text: How can you support an estimator or project manager to keep all of their plates spinning? The real answer is, however you choose to design it. I know it can be challenging and comes with a lot of risk of exposure and money at stake. A Personal Story: I just got off the phone with a company who had been using personality profile tests for the last few years and were not seeing great success from it. Their project managers were under performing for the normally high standards of the company. So they tried something different.
cards.title: Three Barriers That Stop Contractors from Profits reference 11

cards.text: They hired a project manager who scored high on the test as a strong sales personality. Instantly, his gross profits starting coming in 20 points higher than anyone else's on his team. Here's the Real Problem: When it comes to maintaining a high profit margin, getting two contractors to agree about what works or how it's done is hard, if not impossible. The reality is what works for one contractor maybe not work for you because of the differences in volume, type of work or other possible factors.
cards.title: Three Barriers That Stop Contractors from Profits reference 12

cards.text: Here's How to Get Around This: Of course, there are things you can learn from the study of how other companies tackle problems like this. But ultimately, in order for you to maintain consistent high gross profit margins, you must know what your costs are and you must be rigorously aware of your financials. It's also important for you to be watching your overall gross profit margins and the person running your work needs to be completely aware of the costs on every single job and how it impacts their gross profits every single day.
cards.title: Three Barriers That Stop Contractors from Profits reference 13

cards.text: The best examples I see of this are project managers who keep a running sheet of the total value of the job, the costs, materials and running gross profits on a daily basis. This kind of awareness allows them to drive their scores where they want them to go. What you measure and track, grows. This is a way of being responsible before and during the job, rather than waiting to see how it all turns out at the end. Your Next Steps
cards.title: Three Barriers That Stop Contractors from Profits reference 14

cards.text: Real Accountability Workbook Instructions 1. Start with the Course Modules: As you begin each three Steps to Power online course module, refer to the corresponding section in the workbook. Each section complements the online content. 2. Complete the Exercises: Each module in the workbook includes "Take Action" exercises to deepen your understanding and apply what you've learned. Complete these after each lesson to solidify your learning and track your progress. 3. Reflect and Set Goals: At the end of each section, use the reflection prompts to assess what you've learned and how it applies to your work. Set goals for how you will implement the strategies covered in the course.
cards.title: Real Accountability Workbook reference 1

cards.text: 4. Use as a Reference: The workbook will be a valuable resource after completing the course. Refer to it when applying the principles in your work or when seeking a refresher on key concepts. 5. Engage with Your Team: If the course is part of a team initiative, use the guide to facilitate discussions and align your team's actions with the concepts you've learned. 6. Track Your Progress: Use the workbook as a personal log to track your development throughout the course. Revisit your goals and reflections regularly to measure your growth and stay aligned with the course's objectives.
cards.title: Real Accountability Workbook reference 2

cards.text: Using the workbook alongside the online course will maximize your learning experience and gain practical tools for transforming your work and performance. Directions: Work with your team to select the accountabilities best suited for each individual, the team, and the overall business. Use the GNA Accountability Tracking Spreadsheet (available for download in the course) to document your work. Give each person an opportunity to choose for themselves. Accountability: an opportunity to report-to account or to say what someone has done. They encompass every task performed in the company. Ensure that every action, task, and needed outcome in the whole business is assigned and held inside a specific accountability such as marketing, sales, business development, production, and or project management.
cards.title: Real Accountability Workbook reference 3

cards.text: Review and discuss each task thoroughly, ensuring clarity and alignment among all team members. Questions: 1. Did each person choose their own accountability with their team, or was it assigned to them? 2. Does the person holding each accountability have the right skills to execute successfully? 3. Did the people currently holding each accountability choose the whole of the accountability, including all the needed actions and results to be successful, or do they feel like some of it was forced on them? When you're ready, head back to the online course to learn more about How to Design Metrics.
cards.title: Real Accountability Workbook reference 4

cards.text: Defining Metrics for Accountability Directions: In this section, you will design metrics that directly support the success of each accountability in your team. Begin by looking at the intended results for each accountability-what does success look like if the task is performed at its best? 1. Define Metrics: Create challenging but achievable metrics for each accountability. Please make sure they are specific, measurable, and realistic, allowing for team autonomy in planning and executing actions. 2. Track Metrics: Once you've defined your metrics, add them to your Accountability Tracking Spreadsheet. This will help you monitor progress and ensure your team is aligned with the intended outcomes.
cards.title: Real Accountability Workbook reference 5

cards.text: Remember, the metrics you design will create the future direction of the business and become a core part of how you track and improve performance, driving your team toward success. 1. Do you have benchmarks for what you really want as an outcome, or are you settling for targets that are safer, more predictable, and easily attainable? 2. Is the target goal challenging, in that it might take a few months to achieve, yet doable? 3. Do any team members have target metrics they achieve every week or every month? If so, set up new ones. 4. Do all team members have metric target goals that are aligned with the company's vision?
cards.title: Real Accountability Workbook reference 6

cards.text: 7. Are there important areas of your business operations in which you do not have target metrics? 8. Do you have the best thought-out metrics for each person, or have you been reasonably safe in targeting for less than what you really want and need? When ready, head back to the online course to learn more about How to Construct Reports. Reports Directions: Construct simple and clear reports for each participating team member. Follow these steps to ensure your reports are effective and transparent: 1. Construct a Report for Each Person: Design a report for each member of the team outlining the task/responsibility and results for each team member.
cards.title: Real Accountability Workbook reference 7

cards.text: 2. Keep It Simple and Clear: Focus on simplicity. Each report should be easy to read and understand, avoiding unnecessary details or complex formats. Aim for transparency so everyone can quickly see the key facts in one minute at most. 3. Highlight Results: The report should clearly show the metrics for results achieved. 4. Use Timeframes to Show Trends: Include past, present, and future data to give a clear picture of progress over time. This will help the team track trends and stay focused on long-term goals. Keep it simple; use a 3 or 4-month view.
cards.title: Real Accountability Workbook reference 8

cards.text: 5. Ensure visibility and transparency of Issues: If the reporting is clear, any breakdowns, issues, or challenges will be easily identifiable. This allows for faster problem-solving and course correction. By following these steps, your reports will keep everyone on the same page and empower the team to take ownership of their tasks, leading to greater success and alignment. Note: In the online course you will find a download: GNA Sample Reports.zip These are examples only. Please use the reports as a reference to guide and design your own reports. cards.title: Revised Seminar Posts reference 1

cards.text: If you can't take a 2-week vacation without everything falling apart, you don't own a business. You own a job that pays you less per hour than your lead carpenter. I've spent 30 years helping construction owners build actual businesses. The difference isn't size. It's systems. One sells for 8x EBITDA. The other? Maybe 2x if they're lucky. POST 3 - SPECIFIC PAIN POINT (Friday Week 1) Industry-specific insight that shows expertise Foremen succeed by DOING the work better than everyone else. Managers succeed by getting work DONE through other people. I see construction owners promote their best field guys to management and wonder why everything goes sideways. You just lost a great foreman AND gained a frustrated manager.
cards.title: Revised Seminar Posts reference 2

cards.text: The solution? Hire managers who understand construction but aren't trying to do the work themselves. Your foreman should stay in the field where they're valuable. Your manager should stay in the office where THEY'RE valuable. POST 4 - THE WAKE-UP CALL (Monday Week 2) Create urgency with a relatable story I just got off a call with a contractor who's been in business 20 years. It's the result of building a business where YOU are the system. Every estimate needs your review. Every job site needs your visit. Every problem needs your solution. You're not running a construction company. You're running a very expensive consulting practice.
cards.title: Revised Seminar Posts reference 3

cards.text: The good news? This is fixable. The bad news? It requires you to stop being the hero. POST 5 - THE CALL TO ACTION (Wednesday Week 2) Final push to workshop with clear next step Construction owners: Stop posting jobs you can't fill. Start building a culture people don't want to leave. Good people exist. They just don't want to work for chaos. If your turnover is high, ask yourself: → Do people know what success looks like? → Can they make decisions without asking you first? → Do they see a path to grow their skills and income? cards.text: Hello, if your reading this letter you're likely a business owner in restoration with all the challenges thereof. Every business owner wants the best for his business, and they want a profitable business that's challenging but still doable in a 40 to 50 work week….Ideal right? Where it starts getting confusing is how do you do that when you have 20 to 30 employees or more? That's where we can go to work, I can help you with a step by step process that builds functional behavior and accountability right into the culture of your business. Because, where you have functional behavior and accountability, you will have PROFITS!
cards.title: The Facts of Business Sales Letter reference 1

cards.text: Fact: There is a science to Performance. Just as there is in sports, there are things you can do in your business that supports the discretionary effort of each key staff. Discretionary effort is defined as what people do when you're not right there telling them what to do. That's what we call it when each person gives their best effort in every circumstance.
cards.title: The Facts of Business Sales Letter reference 2

cards.text: Fact: Similarly there are things you can do that gets in the way of each person giving their best effort. No one wakes up in the morning and says, I think I will do some stuff to slow my people down today…no one says that. However it happens because owners don't realize it when they do those things. Fact: Where many owners breakdown is in not getting really clear about what works and what doesn't work, the very common result being that many businesses have some things that are working to support performance and some things that are not working to support performance.
cards.title: The Facts of Business Sales Letter reference 3

cards.text: Fact: When you give your key employees everything they need to get their job done to the best of their ability, productivity goes up, and profits follow. Like a strong engine running on all cylinders, your business is capable of seriously good profitability. You just need to design and tune it to produce that way for you.
cards.title: The Facts of Business Sales Letter reference 4

cards.text: Fact: Your employees will play whatever game you set up. Your responsible for setting it up so that's it's a win / win for everyone. The counterintuitive thing here is employees really want to get their job done to the best of their ability, they are far more satisfied in doing so. Successful companies have figured out how to hire well, and give their key employees huge responsibilities, accountabilities, and the freedom to excel. Less successful companies, companies that are struggling in various parts of the business, misunderstand how to manage in a way that unleashes each person's potential.
cards.title: The Facts of Business Sales Letter reference 5

cards.text: Fact: It takes the same effort, just as much energy, to do things the right way as it takes to do things the other way. Every business is slightly different in its size, challenges, number of employees…. so call me today to find out what this can look like for you. Or, send in the questionnaire included, and I will call you back for an appt to discuss your biggest challenges.
cards.title: The Facts of Business Sales Letter reference 6

cards.text: Video 1 - "Still Working Weekends After 15 Years" Title: Still Working Nights and Weekends After 15 Years? Script: "If you've been in business 10, 15, even 20 years… but you're still working nights and weekends, let me ask you this: What did you actually build? Because if your business can't run without you - if every job, every question, every fire lands on your lap - you don't own a business. You own a job. And a stressful one at that.
cards.title: 90 Second Video Scripts reference 1

cards.text: You should be able to step back, take a weekend, take a vacation… and know things are still running smooth, jobs are getting done, clients are being served, and money's coming in. That's what we help construction business owners fix. We help you build a motivated, results-driven team. Install the systems. Make more profit in fewer hours. And most importantly - turn your business into something that's worth 3x to 8x what it is today. If you're done with 70-hour weeks, we should talk. Book a free consultation today, and let's talk about how to build a business that works without you."
cards.title: 90 Second Video Scripts reference 2

cards.text: Video 2 - "Want to Retire But the Business Needs You" Title: Can You Retire Without the Business Falling Apart? Script: "Here's a tough question: What would happen if you disappeared from your business for 30 days? Would everything still run smoothly? Or would everything stall? If you want to retire someday - or even slow down - but the business still needs you every single day, you've got a big problem. At some point, you need to stop being the center of everything. That's exactly what we help construction owners do.
cards.title: 90 Second Video Scripts reference 3

cards.text: Inside our 12-month mastermind, we walk you through how to build leadership underneath you… delegate decisions… increase profits… and get your business in shape to sell when the time is right. Whether you want to retire in 2 years or 10, now is the time to make it salable - and valuable. If you're tired of the business depending on you, book a free consultation today. We'll show you how to shift from being the operator to being the true owner."
cards.title: 90 Second Video Scripts reference 4

cards.text: Video 3 - "Busy But Barely Profitable" Title: Busy All the Time… But Where's the Profit? Script: "You're booked out. Your crews are working. The jobs keep coming in. But when you look at the numbers at the end of the month… there's barely anything left over. Sound familiar? You're not alone. A lot of construction owners think being busy means they're doing well. But busy doesn't mean profitable. Busy can just mean burned out. The truth is - you need a system for profit. We help owners like you plug the leaks, price jobs properly, and build teams that produce results without constant supervision.
cards.title: 90 Second Video Scripts reference 5

cards.text: And when you dial that in? You work fewer hours. You increase profit margins. And your business becomes worth 3x to 8x more. If you're ready to stop working like crazy for crumbs, let's talk. Book a free consultation today - we'll help you make busy actually mean profitable."
cards.title: 90 Second Video Scripts reference 6

cards.text: Video 4 - "Can't Find or Keep Good People" Title: Why You Can't Find (or Keep) Good People Script: "If your biggest headache right now is people… you're not alone. You can't find the right ones. And when you do - they leave. And that constant cycle? It's not just frustrating. It's expensive. And it keeps you stuck doing more than you should. The problem usually isn't just the labor pool. It's the business systems - or lack of them. We help construction business owners create a culture that attracts and keeps great people. With clear roles. Real accountability. And an environment where the right folks want to stay.
cards.title: 90 Second Video Scripts reference 7

cards.text: That gives you a team that's efficient, results-driven, and doesn't rely on you to move every project forward. If you're tired of rehiring every six months, let's fix it. Call us today for a free consultation and let's build the team your business needs."
cards.title: 90 Second Video Scripts reference 8

cards.text: Video 5 - "Inconsistent Crews or Locations" Title: Why One Crew Succeeds-and the Other Doesn't Script: "You've got one crew that always gets it done. Clean. On time. On budget. And another that… well, doesn't. Same company. Same jobs. Totally different outcomes. What gives? Here's the truth: consistency isn't a personality trait - it's a systems issue. In our mastermind, we help you create standards, processes, and performance tracking that makes every crew efficient, every time. And when you get this right? You get fewer callbacks, happier clients, more profit - and a business that can scale without chaos.
cards.title: 90 Second Video Scripts reference 9

cards.text: Video 6 - "No Financial Clarity" Title: Are You Actually Making Money? Script: "Let me ask you something: Can you open your books right now and tell me your real profit margin? Most construction owners can't - and that's dangerous. We see it all the time: jobs are flying, crews are busy, invoices are going out… but the owner still has no idea if the business is actually making money. Inside our mastermind, we help you get financial visibility - fast. You'll learn how to track the right numbers, identify where profit's leaking, and finally understand what's working and what's not. More clarity. More profit. Fewer surprises.
cards.title: 90 Second Video Scripts reference 10

cards.text: Video 7 - "I Make Every Decision" Title: Why You're Still the Only One Making Decisions Script: "If everything still comes back to you - every decision, every problem, every approval - then your business isn't scalable. It's stuck. You're the bottleneck. The reason? You don't have real systems. Or leadership under you. That's what we help you build in our 12-month mastermind. You'll learn how to create real decision-making structures. Empower the right people. And finally stop being the only one who can say 'yes.' That means fewer hours. Higher profits. And a business that's actually worth something - not just a stressful job in disguise.
cards.title: 90 Second Video Scripts reference 11

cards.text: Video 8 - "Still Doing the Work" Title: Are You a CEO… or the Most Expensive Employee? Script: "Are you still out in the field every day? Still running the jobs? Still swinging the hammer? If so, you're not building a business. You're working a job - just one that happens to have your name on the paperwork. It's time to get out of the weeds. In our mastermind, we help you shift from doing the work to leading the business. You'll delegate with confidence. Build a team that executes. And create systems that let you grow, withoutdoing more yourself. The result?
cards.title: 90 Second Video Scripts reference 12

cards.text: You'll work fewer hours, make more profit, and build a business worth 3x to 8x what it's worth today. Call us today for a free consultation, and let's talk about how to finally step into the CEO role your business needs."
cards.title: 90 Second Video Scripts reference 13

cards.text: Video 9 - "Close Rate Sucks" Title: Your Close Rate Sucks - And Nobody Knows Why Script: "You're bidding jobs like crazy. But they're just… not closing. And nobody seems to know why. That's not just a sales problem - that's a business problem. Inside our mastermind, we help you build a repeatable, trackable sales process that actually works. So your team knows what to say. When to follow up. And how to close jobs without cutting your price. You'll go from chasing every lead… to confidently closing high-margin work with the right clients. If your close rate is costing you money and momentum, let's fix it. Call us today for a free consultation and we'll show you how."
cards.title: 90 Second Video Scripts reference 14

cards.text: Video 10 - "Fighting Fires All Day" Title: Too Busy Fighting Fires to Grow the Business? Script: "Let me guess - your day starts with a plan… And by 9AM, that plan is out the window. A crew's late. A client's upset. A supplier dropped the ball. Suddenly, you're back in firefighter mode. And that big idea you had? The growth plan, the strategy, the next phase? It's buried under a pile of emergencies - again. The truth is, if you're always fighting fires, your business isn't running right. You don't need to work harder. You need to lead differently.
cards.title: 90 Second Video Scripts reference 15

cards.text: In our 12-month mastermind, we help construction business owners like you: ✅ Eliminate recurring problems with real systems ✅ Build a team that solves problems before they hit your desk ✅ Free up time and headspace to focus on growth ✅ And turn the business into something that's actually worth selling someday - 3x to 8x what it's worth now You can't grow while you're in survival mode. And you don't have to live in crisis. If you're ready to get out of firefighting mode and into growth mode - call us for a free consultation. We'll help you build the business that doesn't need you to save the day, every day."

cards.text: I'm sending you this email because I've met you at a conference or we've connected over the years and you gave me your business card and asked me to email you. I'm committed to sending you information on ways to help increase your net profits. Each week I'm going to send you some tips on ways to make your business run and grow without you being a major part of it. I'll also send you emails about new training courses and resources from time when I know they'll benefit you. If for some reason you don't want to receive emails with ways to increase your business' net profits, then simple click here to unsubscribe now.
cards.title: Two Challenges to Great Employee Performance reference 1

cards.text: Here's a taste of some of the knowledge I'll be sharing with you: Have you ever had a situation where you had a loyal employee who has been with you for years, they were trained and knew how to do their job yet, their productivity was really low. How can you get this person to increase their productivity? Real accountability is another way of saying, get their buy in. Let me make this plain and simple because this is a powerful tool to help your employees get focused. This is critically important because real accountability is a personal choice. It's not you forcing them to complete a task.
cards.title: Two Challenges to Great Employee Performance reference 2

cards.text: If you're forcing people to do things, their productivity will always be low over the long-term. But when you give your employees a choice and get their buy in, they will jump through hoops to hit the goals because they feel that were part of the decision making process. When you can get their buy in, they will have more trust and respect for you because you have trust and respect for them by asking for their buy in. This is the difference between being a boss and a leader. That's a whole topic in and of itself.
cards.title: Two Challenges to Great Employee Performance reference 3

cards.text: The problem is too many business owners don't get their employees buy in and/or they assume the employee has already made a choice. When this happens your employees feel burdened with choice they didn't make and they start to resent and resist you. This then leads to a situation where you feel like you have to push them harder to get anything done. This is why I want you to get your employees to buy in to what needs to happen in your business. I have never encountered an employee who when given a choice didn't choose their own accountabilities. Give people a choice to choose their own accountabilities and they will step up to meet their expectations every time.
cards.title: Two Challenges to Great Employee Performance reference 4

cards.text: In fact, when given the choice, you will be surprised at how willing your employees are to take on whatever accountabilities they need to make things work for everyone. Now that you understand the two challenges to having great employee performance and how to solve them, I'd like to invite you to get even more advanced help to grow your company. Check out the 5 Deadly Hiring Mistakes Most Contractors Make: HYPERLINK "http://bit.ly/the5hiringmistakes" http://bit.ly/the5hiringmistakes After 20 years, I've learned when you can find and hire good people, it's really easy to grow a great and profitable company.
cards.title: Two Challenges to Great Employee Performance reference 5

This is the type of information I'll be sharing with you on a weekly basis to help you increase your company's net profits.
